name: mcp-patchbay
description: Hosts your MCP servers and lets Claude switch them on and off mid-session, with a person approving risky ones.
long_description:
mcp-patchbay is an MCP server that hosts other MCP servers as child processes. Claude sees five small tools (`servers`, `enable`, `disable`, `restart` and `info`). When it enables a server, that server starts and its tools appear straight away; when it disables one, they disappear. Servers you mark `confirm` need a person, not the model, to approve each enable.

On first start it creates a private config with no servers at `~/.config/mcp-patchbay/servers.json`. Add your connectors to that file as the README's Quick start shows, then turn the extension off and on again.

It collects no data and sends nothing to its publisher. The servers you configure are separate programs with their own privacy policies.

tools.name: servers
tools.description: List the hosted MCP servers and their state

tools.name: enable
tools.description: Turn on a hosted MCP server, asking a person first for confirm servers

tools.name: disable
tools.description: Turn off a hosted MCP server

tools.name: info
tools.description: Show a hosted server's description, policy, state and instructions

config_path.title: Config file
config_path.description: The patchbay's servers.json. At the default path it is created on first start with no servers; any other path must already exist.
